STS2_WINE_FOX_ADDONS_EVENT_MIDNIGHT_DINE:
The smell of [gold]hot oil[/gold] drifts down the alley. You follow it around the corner and find a wooden door left ajar, [orange]dim yellow light[/orange] spilling through the gap along with the sound of an iron ladle scraping a pot.

There is only one table inside. At the stove stands a [green]fox-eared cook[/green], her back to you, and she does not turn around.

[b]"Sit down. What'll you have?"[/b]

You eat until you could not fit another bite.

Only when you set down the bowl do you notice the stove is cold and the pot is empty.

But your stomach is full all the same. [sine]You decide not to think about it.[/sine]

The cook wraps something in oiled paper and presses it into your hands.

[b]"Open it when you're hungry."[/b]

The paper is still warm. When you look back from the mouth of the alley, the door is gone.

You shake your head and step back over the threshold.

As you leave the alley, the light behind you goes out.
STS2_WINE_FOX_ADDONS_EVENT_SPIRE_VILLAGE:
Halfway up the stairs the trees pull back and a [gold]village[/gold] comes into view — a few crooked wooden houses, carrots just coming up in the plots, lanterns strung from wooden poles.

Villagers lean out of their doorways, [sine]hmm-ing[/sine], and crowd around to push you toward the counter. A handful of goods are laid out, and every price tag is absurd.

[b]"Hmm!"[/b]
(They seem to believe the prices are perfectly fair.)
Point out every absurd price. Gain [gold]Emerald Badge[/gold].

You count out [blue]{Gold}[/blue] [gold]Gold[/gold] and line the coins up on the counter.

The villagers nod, [sine]hmm hmm[/sine], tuck the coins into their aprons, and solemnly hand you a piece of goods — the wrapping still carries the last buyer's name.

[b]"Hmm-mm!"[/b]

You point at the tags and list every problem: the price, the weight, the quality.

The villagers listen quietly, glance at one another, then pull an [gold]Emerald Badge[/gold] out from under the counter and pin it to your collar.

[sine]From then on, the [blue]Merchant[/blue]'s hand hesitates when it reaches for one of your cards.[/sine]

You stop arguing, sweep the [gold]emeralds[/gold] off the counter and into your bag.

The village [red]bell[/red] rings. One by one the doors shut, and eyes behind the curtains watch you leave.

And that [red]Greed[/red] you picked up is not something you can put back down.
